extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Early calculating devices — Abacus: ancient device with beads on rods, used for addition and subtraction. Napier's bones: rods invented by John Napier for multiplication and division. Pascaline: mechanical calculator invented by Blaise Pascal for addition and subtraction using dials. (2) Mechanical and electromechanical devices — Difference Engine: designed by Charles Babbage for polynomial calculations. Analytical Engine: also by Babbage, designed for general-purpose computation — the first design for a programmable computer, earning Babbage the title 'Father of the Computer'. Tabulating Machine: invented by Herman Hollerith, used punched cards for the US Census, later became IBM. (3) Generations of computers — First (1940s-1950s): vacuum tubes, very large, ENIAC. Second (1950s-1960s): transistors, smaller and faster. Third (1960s-1970s): integrated circuits (IC), even smaller. Fourth (1970s-present): microprocessors, personal computers, laptops. Fifth (present and beyond): artificial intelligence, quantum computing, natural language processing. (4) Characteristics, advantages, limitations — Characteristics: speed, accuracy, storage, diligence, versatility, connectivity. Advantages: fast, accurate, store huge data, work 24/7, do many tasks. Limitations: no intelligence of their own, cannot make decisions, depend on electricity, need human instructions, cannot think or feel. Misconceptions: 'the abacus was invented by a single person' (WRONG — the abacus is an ancient device with no single inventor, used by many civilizations), 'Babbage built the Analytical Engine' (WRONG — Babbage DESIGNED the Analytical Engine but it was never fully built in his lifetime due to technology limitations), 'transistors were used in first generation computers' (WRONG — first generation used vacuum tubes; transistors came in the second generation), 'computers can think like humans' (WRONG — computers follow instructions; they cannot think, feel, or make decisions on their own), 'newer generations are always completely different' (WRONG — each generation builds on the previous one, improving speed, size, and efficiency).
